name: Double Outlet Right Ventricle with Non-Committed Subpulmonary Ventricular Septal Defect
aliases: Double outlet right ventricle, subpulmonary VSD variant

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Heart Disease Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of both great arteries arising predominantly from the right ventricle confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Identification of a non-committed subpulmonary ventricular septal defect distinct from the outlet septum
Signs of cyanotic congenital heart disease including central cyanosis and heart murmur

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic or imaging confirmation of both great arteries arising from the right ventricle plus identification of a non-committed subpulmonary VSD
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cardiac catheterization may be required for detailed anatomical assessment and surgical planning.

pathognomonic.notes: Bluish discoloration of lips and mucous membranes due to right-to-left shunting

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic ejection murmur at left upper sternal border
pathognomonic.notes: Due to turbulent flow across the pulmonary outflow tract
searchTerms: heart murmur heard at upper left chest
systolic murmur at left upper sternum
ejection murmur at left upper chest

common.notes: Reduced exercise capacity due to hypoxemia
Increased respiratory rate secondary to cardiac insufficiency

common.symptomName: Heart failure signs (e.g., hepatomegaly, peripheral edema)
common.notes: Due to volume overload and ventricular dysfunction
searchTerms: signs of heart failure like swollen liver and legs
fluid buildup causing hepatomegaly and edema
heart failure symptoms with peripheral swelling
clubbing with blue fingers or toes
finger or toe discoloration and swelling

occasional.notes: Atrial or ventricular arrhythmias due to cardiac structural abnormalities
Secondary erythrocytosis due to chronic hypoxia
Transient loss of consciousness related to hypoxia or arrhythmia
Signs related to elevated pulmonary artery pressures
searchTerms: symptoms of high lung blood pressure

occasional.notes: Increased susceptibility due to pulmonary congestion

rare.notes: Paradoxical embolism due to right-to-left shunting
Infective endocarditis risk due to abnormal cardiac anatomy

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit and hemoglobin due to secondary polycythemia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating both great arteries arising from right ventricle and non-committed subpulmonary VSD
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical delineation
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with chromosomal anomalies in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of overriding aorta rather than both great arteries arising from right ventricle
Subaortic VSD rather than non-committed subpulmonary VSD
Characteristic boot-shaped heart on chest X-ray
Aorta arises from right ventricle and pulmonary artery from left ventricle (discordant ventriculoarterial connection)
Absence of VSD or presence of subpulmonary VSD but with different arterial arrangement
Clinical presentation with severe cyanosis in neonatal period

redFlags: Severe central cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate or infant
Sudden onset of neurological deficits suggestive of embolic stroke
references: Anderson RH, et al. Double outlet right ventricle: anatomy and diagnosis. Heart. 2014;100(7): 555-562.
Moller JH, et al. Congenital Heart Disease in Adults. Circulation. 2013;128(21): 2345-2355.
Orphanet Report Series: Double outlet right ventricle with non-committed subpulmonary ventricular septal defect. Orphanet. 2023.
